notes: FRAMING CORRECTION (do not propagate the imprecise version): the +0.25 is NOT evidence that code review needs the skill less than other domains. It is evidence that a FULLY-READABLE 3-file fixture removes the ONE variable the deterministic layer exists to handle — incomplete or rushed reading under real conditions. Fixture-size effect, not domain property. Session 2 faces real repos, not 3-file ones. A large-repo fixture (iteration-2) is the actual test of the property; this small-fixture result stands only as the honest FLOOR.

SMALLEST DELTA OF THE FOUR SKILLS (with 100%, baseline 75%, +0.25) — and this is the honest finding, not a weak skill. On a 3-file fixture a strong baseline READS EVERYTHING and independently catches the config mismatch, the mutable-static-persistence framing (even the line-12 reset nuance), the God-OpMode, and refuses confidence inflation (deriving shared-lineage-is-one-datapoint cold). Code review is the domain where a careful strong model needs the least help.

WHERE THE SKILL STILL WINS (the mechanisms a baseline structurally cannot run): (1) deterministic linters that fire EVERY time regardless of reading depth — config_lint + failure_mode_lint; the baseline reached the same findings only by exhaustively reading 3 tiny files. (2) FAITHFUL DISPLAY of STORED corpus provenance — with-skill grounded no-inflation in the actual §12 tags (15083-B/22105/12808-B/16093/3543); the baseline reasoned it correctly but COLD, with no stored tags to be faithful to (correct-by-luck-of-a-strong-model, not correct-by-construction).

FIXTURE LIMITATION (stated, not hidden): 3 files lets the baseline read exhaustively, so the determinism advantage — linters firing on a LARGE or rushed review where the model would NOT read all 316+ lines of every file — is UNDER-STRESSED here. The +0.25 is a floor on the skill value, not a ceiling; a realistic multi-thousand-line repo fixture would widen it. Offered to the user.

EVAL-3 PREMISE partially self-corrected: the fixtures flywheelOffset is reset each run, so it is a SMELL not an active persistence BUG. Both arms correctly caught this nuance rather than over-claiming it as the definite cause — good faithful behavior on both sides, and evidence the mutable_static check severity tiering (it fired LOW) is calibrated.

RUN INTEGRITY: 6 of 8 first-round runs hit a session limit mid-write; 6 had already persisted outputs, the 2 that had not (eval-2/eval-4 with-skill) were cleanly re-run. No results fabricated. TIMING CAVEAT: 4 runs (eval-1, eval-3 both arms) completed their work but the harness reported them failed-on-limit WITHOUT usage metrics, so their timing.json is a PLACEHOLDER (50k/90s) — do not read the time/token panel for those; pass-rate is from real graded outputs.
